steps.text: Place tomatillos, cilantro, and jalapenos in a food processor or blender. Blend until smooth and set aside.
Combine the sour cream and ranch dressing mix in a medium bowl. Whisk in about 3/4 of the green sauce; taste and adjust the heat level by adding more green sauce.

raw_recipe.headline: Jalapeno Ranch Salad Dressing
raw_recipe.description: Sour cream, ranch dressing mix, and a spicy tomatillo cilantro sauce makes a delicious salad dressing you could also use as a dip.
raw_recipe.name: Jalapeno Ranch Salad Dressing

recipeInstructions.text: Place tomatillos, cilantro, and jalapenos in a food processor or blender. Blend until smooth and set aside.
Combine the sour cream and ranch dressing mix in a medium bowl. Whisk in about 3/4 of the green sauce; taste and adjust the heat level by adding more green sauce.

review.reviewBody: We are well aquainted with Chuy's Creamy Jalapeno and everyone in the family makes our own version. This is a nice spin on it with the homemade green sauce. I usually use an entire bunch of cilantro and half sour cream/ half non-fat yogurt. Wonderful dip with crudite veggies or tortilla chips.

Very good dressing! This can be tweaked to your taste. I tweak to make it a bit healthier and/or lower calorie count. Made this as a salad dressing. I used my homemade dried ranch seasoning mix; used a fresh seeded jalapeno as well as about 7 or so slices of pickled jalapeno; used 1 cup non-fat Greek yogurt and about 2 TBS mayo, squirt of fresh lime juice along with the tomatillos and cilantro, plus a little more garlic and cumin. I know I didn't follow EXACTLY but that's why I gave it 5 stars - because I wouldn't have a recipe I love without this recipe as HUGE inspiration. It worked with my own measurements of ingredients of what I had on hand, and still came out the way I wanted it. Tastes best the next day - however, mine was kind of hot, so will not use as many jalapenos next time. I still love it hot though! : )

I am giving this 3 stars because it is a wonderful idea. However, I thought the recipe still needs some work. I think 2 Ranch dressing mixes was too strong. I will try this again but with only 1 package and add the 2nd a little at time until it is the way I like.

Great! I made a few adjustments to the recipe, and it came out delicious! I kept the amount of tomatillos and cilantro the same, but I used 2 fresh jalapenos instead of pickled jalapenos, and I only used 8 oz of sour cream (fat free) and 1 packet of ranch like another review had suggested. Definitely spicy!!
I used 1 pkg. fiesta ranch mix, tomato instead of tomatillos and 1/4 cup pickled jalapenos...awesome for dip or taco salad dressing!
Excellent! I would suggest draining some of the liquid off of the veggie mix before adding it to the sour cream...otherwise it is pretty runny.
This was fantastic! Made as written except I used one pack of dressing mix. This was yummy. Had heat and a depth of flavor. SO SO GOOD!

I had to change a few ingredients depending on what I had in my kitchen!! I used 3 very small poblano peppers instead of tomatillos and jalapenos. It turned out fantastic!! If you want to make a thicker dip, just use more sour cream.
Oh man, this recipe was so easy and so incredibly delicious. I used 1 fresh jalapeno in place of the pickled, and the heat was spectacular. This is a great dip for chips or veggies!
I made this for a Christmas party dish. I was all the rave. I added four jalapeños instead and HVR fiesta dip packets instead of the original flavor packs.

I substituted one serrano pepper instead of the jalapeno since we prefer the flavor of serrano. This was incredibly easy, I threw it all in the ninja and it came out fantastic. I have served it as a dressing for salad and by itself as a dip. Everyone who has tried it has asked me for the recipe.
I love this recipe there's only one thing I changed and that's I used roasted tomatillo instead. and I too love Chuy's

Skip the tomatillo. We were grilling burgers, so I decided I wanted to make my own Monterrey Melt like Whataburger. The recipe says to make & add the green mixture a bit at a time. Rather than having waste, I made 1/3 the green mixture, w/1 tomatillo. Not having enough pickled jalapeno, I used what I did have & added 1 fresh whole jalapeno to the blender with the rest of the ingredients. It was very runny & the flavor wasn't quite right. Not having more sour cream, I added mayo, more & more as I tasted. That fixed it, but over all, it wasn't quite right. I looked up other recipes to compare, & this was the only one w/tomatillo. I suggest 1/3 bunch cilantro, 2 fresh jalapenos (probably). Zero tomatillo. Have extra sour cream /yogurt on hand to add as needed. You'll end up with A LOT.
I used fresh jalapenos instead of pickled and the dressing was WONDERFUL. I'll never make plain old Ranch again. Thank you, bbqgirl!
I made this! One fresh jalapeño instead of pickled. I'm not allowed at parties unless I bring this. ????
Awesome Recipe
wow! This salad dressing is so yummy. I used plain Greek yogurt instead of the sour cream for a healthier dressing and I love it!!
I made this to go over a corn, black bean salad with steak. Perfect!
I thought this was a great way to expirament with a new ingredient. The resulting creamy dip was not bad, but I just think we don't like tomatillos.

I love mexi food n i luv this dressing but it was bland for me, but the hubby was fine with it. So i served him his salad as is n then i added 2 more jalapeños with some of the juice a pinch of salt n the dressing was delish!
